Official purpose (project sheet and budget book): 'facility condition assessments, capital planning, estimating, managing project and construction timelines, managing the capital budget, and ensuring the effective design, implementation, and construction of various capital projects.' The five-year plan keeps this at $23.0M a year.

side.label: CPS capital expenditure data shows 17 'CIP Management' projects with $31,345,033 of FY2026 spending, mostly one citywide management project ($28,913,238). It is shared across capital funds, so it is not tied to this $23.0M line

nodes.name: Teacher pension levy paid to the Chicago Teachers' Pension Fund
nodes.note: Budget-only line: a reserve, not a payment. Split below is an estimate (proxy), see each piece.

nodes.name: Reserve for non-teacher staff pensions (MEABF)
nodes.note: Reserve in case CPS must repay the City for non-teacher pensions. A separate $175M repayment to the City is not in the budget. Members and averages are for all City and CPS members, so no split by dollars is shown. CPS budgets this reserve in case it must repay the City for non-teacher staff pensions. The budget book says a $175M reimbursement depends on new revenue (budget book p.15).

side.label: MEABF covers City and CPS non-teacher workers. CPS employees are about 64% of active members (Forecast 2027 p.22).

nodes.why: This is money set aside in case the school district has to repay the City for the pensions of non-teacher staff, and nobody has decided yet if it will be paid.

nodes.name: Pension reserve in the general fund (a reservation, not a payment)

nodes.name: State's share of the teacher pension that schools are not charged for
